key_insight: A D-gun applied Al2O3–TiO2 ceramic coating significantly improves the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and random forest best predicts wear from sliding conditions.
engineering_relevance: This work supports using detonation-sprayed ceramic coatings to extend the service life of Ti-6Al-4V components in aerospace, biomedical, and marine tribological applications.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3–TiO2 coating to Ti-6Al-4V by detonation gun spray.
Evaluated wear with ASTM G99 pin-on-disc tests under 40–100 N, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min against EN31 steel.
Trained ANN, KNN, and random forest models to map sliding parameters to wear.
evidence_signal: Experimental microscopy showed reduced wear and tribo-layer formation on coated samples, while random forest had the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a limited test matrix and a specific coating/process window, so broader generalization to other loads, speeds, substrates, or service environments still needs validation.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
